newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.

text.p: In the South, rice prices were steady, USDA said. Long grain milled rice prices were selling mostly at $19.50 per cwt, medium grain traded mostly at $18.00-19.00, second heads were steady to $1.00 higher and brewers remain in very tight supply with few quotes at $14.50-15.50. Rice by-products were mostly steady.

In California, rice prices were steady with medium grain selling mostly at $19.50. Rice bran was steady to $2.00 lower. There were 220,560 cwt of U.S. medium grain rice inspected for export for the week to Jan 4, 1997. The yearly total since Oct 1, 1996 is 3,339,665 cwt compared to 2,443,152 cwt a year ago.

California rice ship loadings For the week ending January 4, 1997, at the Port of Sacramento there were no ship loadings; at the port of Stockton the MV Coral loaded 8,900 mt of U.S. No. 1 bagged Medium Grain milled rice and 1,100 mt of second heads destined for Japan.

The following prices were for domestic shipment -- offers, FOB mills, milled rice, dollars per cwt, bagged. (All milled rice grade 2 not to exceed 4 percent brokens, except California grade 1. All second heads grade 4 or better)
